_comment: YTD actuals + full-year forecast overrides for /tax-project. Read-only input; never holds computed results.
_comment_tax_year: The covered year this file is FOR. Optional while the file answers none of the four prior_year_* fields below — every file predating them leaves it null and nothing else here is bound to a year. Once any of them is answered it is REQUIRED and must match --year: those figures are composed under the covered year's own Form 2210 line-8 instructions, so re-running last year's file against this year feeds the wrong return's base to the prior-year prong, and there is no marker left in the output to catch it afterwards. A declared mismatch is always refused, and so is any spelling that is not a plain number — write 2026, never "2026".
_comment_as_of_date: MM-DD the `ytd` figures below are current to — provenance for them, not a run date. null means 'no date attached': the current year then reads as today, a CLOSED year as 12-31. Any other value must be a real MM-DD. A PRESENT but invalid one ("", 0, false, "6/30") is REFUSED in an open year rather than replaced with today's date, because replacing it relabels YTD figures entered as of some other date; in a closed year it degrades to 12-31 under a banner and is never echoed back. Use null to mean absent — an empty string is not the same answer.
_comment_prior_year_form_2210_tax_base: Completed pre-factor prior-year tax constructed under line 8 of the Form 2210 instructions for the covered year. Never enter raw Form 1040 line 24 or Form 2210 line 8 after its 100%/110% factor; leave null when the covered-year line-8 composition is not complete. A base of exactly 0 requires EITHER prior_year_zero_liability_confirmed OR prior_year_return_filed_12_months_confirmed below — two independent statutory routes, either one alone is enough, and neither implies the other. See both comments below before asking about only one. Answering this field makes tax_year above required.
_comment_prior_year_form_2210_agi: AGI from the SAME return prior_year_form_2210_tax_base was composed from (its amendment rule included) — never a different return's AGI, and read off THAT year's own Form 1040 by its printed label: line 11 carries AGI only on the 2020-and-later form. On 2019 AGI is 8b and line 11 is a deduction subtotal; on 2018 AGI is 7 and line 11 is the tax; on 2017 AGI is 37. Every one of those is smaller than AGI, so a mechanical line-11 read passes for under $150,000 and selects the 100% factor where 110% is owed — the required payment a tenth low. Optional: omitting it degrades the prior-year prong to the 100% factor with a flagged 'prior AGI unknown' note rather than guessing.
_comment_prior_year_zero_liability_confi: Set true only after confirming ALL THREE conditions of Sec. 6654(e)(2), and a base of 0 is NOT one of them: the prior year was a full 12-month year, the taxpayer had NO LIABILITY for it, and was a US citizen or resident throughout it. No liability means that year's Form 1040 TOTAL TAX line was 0, or no return was required at all — never prior_year_form_2210_tax_base above, which subtracts refundable credits and reaches 0 on a positive total tax (a $500 SE tax under a $2,000 EIC). Confirming only the 12-month and citizenship halves is what this comment used to ask for, and on an unfiled prior year it zeroes the required annual payment for someone who owes 90% of the current one. It does NOT require that a return was filed. One of the two routes that lets a prior_year_form_2210_tax_base of exactly 0 through (Sec. 6654(e)(2)).
_comment_prior_year_return_filed_12_mont: The OTHER route to a 0 base, and an independent test: set true after confirming the prior year was a full 12-month year AND a return was filed for it. That is Sec. 6654(d)(1)(B)'s closing text, and it carries no citizenship or residency condition — 100%/110% of a 0 prior-year tax is 0, so the required annual payment is 0 by the ordinary prong. Ask about it separately: a taxpayer who cannot affirm the citizenship half of the flag above is still covered by this one, and collapsing the two demanded 90% of the current year from them. Either flag alone is enough; with neither, a 0 base is refused rather than silently accepted.
_comment_foreign_tax_credit_projection: Optional reviewed full-year regular FTC alone while AMT remains unmodeled. Bind tax_year, canonical filing_status, full_year_inputs_confirmed, federal_agi_at_review, taxable_income_at_review, regular_tax_at_review and regular_foreign_tax_credit (allowed amount, including a worked zero, never gross foreign taxes paid). Review eligibility, elections and limits externally for the covered year and record the workpaper in answers.md; see tax-project/references/amt-irmaa.md. Do not combine with amt_projection. A prior AMT credit still requires the full AMT worksheet.
_comment_amt_projection: Reviewed full-year Form 6251 preference, deduction and credit worksheet; see tax-project/references/amt-irmaa.md. Null leaves AMT explicitly unmodeled: federal total and payment targets then exclude it and may be low. A present incomplete or unsupported worksheet refuses computation. No archived ISO spread or guessed zero preferences.
_comment_irmaa_projection: Reviewed full-year Medicare MAGI and beneficiary/coverage worksheet; see tax-project/references/amt-irmaa.md. Premium year is income year+2; CLI reads that premium year's separately fetched tax_law cache. Unpublished or empty future tiers leave the premium estimate unresolved, never replaced by income-year rates. Surcharges stay separate from income tax and payment targets.
_comment_state_projection: Optional dedicated full-year NY/NC forecast; null leaves the state unmodeled. Complete the interview and reviewed worksheet contract in docs/contributing/state-planning.md and tax-project/references/state-estimates.md. Binds tax_year, uppercase filing_status, full-year household residency and projected federal AGI/SE income. All state/local withholding is combined in ytd.state_withholding. Supply completed prior-year estimated-tax base and eligibility, never archived gross tax. Missing local/allocation answers refuse any state balance or payment schedule. Initial reviewed form year: 2025; fetched later-year rates do not authorize a later form.

forecast_overrides._comment: Lumpy/known items entered as FULL-YEAR amounts; NOT annualized. Prefer the capital_gains_short/_long split — short-term gains are ordinary-rate income, and the legacy combined capital_gains field is treated as LONG-term. Supplying both the legacy field and the split is an error.
forecast_overrides._comment_schedule_1a: OBBBA Schedule 1-A total (tips + overtime premium + car-loan + senior), a full-year BELOW-AGI deduction (line 13b, TY2025-2028). Estimate the capped/MAGI-phased amount via compute_schedule_1a; it reduces projected taxable income but NOT AGI (so taxable SS/NIIT are unchanged). Gated off outside TY2025-2028, for MFS, and when the fetched federal.schedule_1a caps are absent.
forecast_overrides._comment_schedule_1a_se_tips: The portion of schedule_1a above that is SELF-EMPLOYED qualified tips from the projected Schedule C business. Form 8995 excludes deducted tip income from QBI, so this amount is also removed from the QBI base (capped at self_employment_net). Leave 0 for W-2 tips or when there is no Schedule C tip income.
forecast_overrides._comment_schedule_a_inputs: Optional complete compute_schedule_a inputs for the projected year, including agi_at_compute and magi_addback. Confirm the year's forecast expenses; use current-year fetched standard deduction and SALT cap. When supplied, the engine re-prices these at projected AGI instead of reading itemized_deductions. Never copy a prior year's inputs unchanged.
forecast_overrides._comment_schedule_a_charitable_limits_co: Set true only after confirming that forecast cash gifts are to public charities and noncash gifts are appreciated property under the Schedule A engine's limits. A binding charitable cap refuses without this confirmation.
forecast_overrides._comment_itemized_deductions: REQUIRED: the itemized deductions you expect to take this year (the Schedule A total, after its caps), or 0 to take the standard deduction. The projection prices from this where it beats the standard deduction, plus from TY2026 the deduction charitable_cash_gifts earns a non-itemizer; null is unanswered and refuses, because the standard deduction in an itemizer's place over-states the tax and every payment the report recommends. Pre-fill from archive/{year-1}/result.json when that return itemized, and adjust for what changed.
forecast_overrides._comment_state_itemized_deductions: REQUIRED for the generic/CA projection: the state itemized deductions you expect (California's Schedule CA total), or 0 for standard. Dedicated NY/NC state_projection uses its own reviewed raw deduction worksheets instead. The state's rules decide whether its choice can differ from federal. null refuses wherever this declared-total path reads it.
forecast_overrides._comment_charitable_cash_gifts: REQUIRED from TY2026: the cash you expect to give to charity this year, or 0 for none. Cash only, and not to a donor-advised fund or a supporting organization. A filer who takes the standard deduction deducts it up to the fetched federal.charitable_non_itemizer cap (Form 1040 line 13c), and the projection counts it when choosing between the standard and itemized deductions; an itemizer's gifts stay inside itemized_deductions too. null refuses, because gifts left out over-state the tax and every payment the report recommends.

recurring_from_prior._comment: Defaults pulled from archive/{year-1}/ by the skill; user-editable. Treated as full-year.

retirement_ytd._comment: Year-to-date retirement contributions for /tax-retirement dashboard. hsa_coverage is 'none'|'self_only'|'family'. plan_allows_after_tax_401k gates Mega Backdoor emission. plan_offers_roth_401k (default true) is load-bearing only for the §603 high-earner case: if a high earner's catch-up MUST be Roth but the plan has no designated Roth source, set this false — affected high earners then cannot make catch-up at all (the dashboard shows base-only, no phantom catch-up). prior_year_fica_wages drives SECURE 2.0 §603 mandatory-Roth-catchup detection (TY2026+): if above the year's fetched indexed threshold, 401(k) catch-up MUST be Roth — supply the FICA wages your PLAN uses for its Roth-catch-up determination per IRC §414(v)(7)(A) (generally the sponsoring employer's, though related common-law employers in the same controlled group may be aggregated under the final regs — confirm with the plan administrator; not your total W-2 across unrelated employers); set to null when unknown to receive a warning rather than silently overstate savings. taxable_compensation caps IRA pool per IRC §219(b)(1)(A) — a retiree with $0 wages has $0 IRA capacity regardless of statutory limit; null triggers a warning. spouse_taxable_compensation enables the §219(c) MFJ spousal IRA exception (non-working spouse can use working spouse's compensation when filing jointly). Roth YTD is part of employee_401k, not additional. Confirm payroll permits pre-tax catch-up after Roth requirement is met. HSA requires eligible_months and december_eligible for unchanged tier, or twelve first-of-month monthly_coverage entries for tier changes; last-month election needs December eligibility and testing-period acknowledgement. A joint spouse catch-up requires independent spouse eligibility inputs.

_paystub_parser_hook: Optional local intake: sh agents/lib/run.sh -m agents.lib.paystub --manifest documents/paystub_manifest.json. Preserves the stable ytd keys and requires explicit job/as-of evidence. See docs/contributing/paystub-intake.md.
